chapter: Learning, lawn parties and band rivalries
title: Solo players, violinists and the Lindsey family
summary: Dawson says there were no solo players, repeats that Palao, Manetta and Bocage were fine sight-readers, and recalls the Lindsey bass player.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Did they ever have any solo players then? No. Did they have any solo players? Solo, no. No. Not as I love, no. No. Tom Mitchell used to tell me about them. He said you didn't have a band on them.

I didn't have a band on them, so. Jimm Apollo was a good violin player, though. He was just like, he was classed just like Emmanuel, uh, Man Manera and, uh, uh, uh, Peter Bocot. All of them good violin players. Sight readers.
What about the Lindsey family? Did you know Johnny and Herbert and their daddy?
Oh, the Lindsey. Johnny Lindsey. Just trying to think of who they played with now. One of them, one of them played, I think one of them played bass upon him and stick.
Yeah, that's Johnny. He's a good bass. Yeah.
